page.layout: One page of text, one column, with Syriac words set in the Latin lines and small reference marks above them. Line 1 is a continuation from the previous page. At the foot, a catchword at the right. Page number at the head.

main_text.p: quiescit in [ɣ] in medio & fine, ut [illegible, ~8 letters] Laloho deo, [illegible, ~6 letters] baja consolatus est.
Quiescit etiam in [ɲ] in medio & fine, ut [illegible, ~10 letters] mecultho cibus, [illegible, ~6 letters] reges.
In [ɨ] in medio tantum, ut [illegible, ~6 letters] verbum.
In [ɵ] in medio & fine, ut [illegible, ~5 letters] arnanum, [illegible, ~5 letters] Deus.
Waw quiescit in vocali [ɬ] idque tantum in medio & fine, ut [illegible, ~9 letters] malcutho et [illegible, ~6 letters] malcu regnum.
In vocali ɵ tantum in nominibus peregrinis, cum (ω) vel (o) aut interdum (υ) Graecum exprimenda sunt, ut [illegible, ~6 letters] παῦλος[?].
Jod quiescit in [ɣ] & [ɲ,] ut [illegible, ~3 letters] mihi, [illegible, ~4 letters] duo.

page.notes: The Syriac words, with their points and small reference marks, could not be read letter by letter; they are marked illegible. The reference letters in square brackets ([ɣ], [ɲ], [ɨ], [ɵ], [ɬ]) are Syriac letters, written here only as approximate symbols. The Greek word is a best reading and should be checked against the scan. The catchword "SECT." is set at the right below the last line.
